summary: The note surveys blockchain startups in Silicon Valley that apply the technology beyond cryptocurrency, in voting, healthcare, supply chains, intellectual property, real estate tokenization, green blockchain and education. It profiles each startup and its founder, highlighting decentralization, transparency and immutability as the core virtues. It concludes that blockchain is a foundational technology comparable to the Internet's evolution, enabling smart contracts, DAOs and user-owned data.
one_line: Profiles of Silicon Valley blockchain startups disrupting voting, healthcare, supply chains, IP, real estate, energy use and education beyond cryptocurrency.
key_facts: SecureChain, founded by Elena Verona, launched operations in October 2023 and provides distributed ledger solutions for secure digital voting systems.
Lifestream presented at the HealthTech Conference on September 15, 2023, with a blockchain platform for secure, real-time access to medical records.
John McKenzie, CEO of Lifestream, envisions a healthcare ecosystem where 'data silos become a thing of the past, and the patients are the true custodians of their health records.'
SupplyBlock, founded by Lisa and Kunal Gupta in late 2023, aims to create an immutable ledger of a product's lifecycle from manufacturer to end consumer, targeting counterfeit products.
CreoMark uses blockchain to register and verify intellectual property rights instantaneously, reducing infringement risk; co-founder Monica Reynolds spoke about the platform.
TokenEstate had its first successful property token launch on November 3, 2023, and its CEO is Alex Kim.
Alex Kim calls TokenEstate's tokenization 'a leap towards financial inclusion.'
GreenLedger, established by environmental scientist Dr. Fiona Carver, develops low-energy blockchain algorithms that minimize energy usage while remaining decentralized.
Edublocks, led by Omar Hassan, records degrees issued by institutions on a public ledger so employers and schools can verify them and falsified credentials are eliminated.
The note names blockchain's core virtues as decentralization, transparency and immutability.
The note says future frontiers include smart contracts that execute without mediators, DAOs without conventional management, and an Internet where users own their data.
The note compares blockchain's trajectory to the Internet's evolution from a military communication tool to a global information network.
